output.title: Atlas SD-WAN Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: SLA class stability and probe tuning
key_facts: Use a probe window of at least five samples so a single 1-second loss spike does not clear the SLA class.
Set the hold-down to 5000 ms before allowing the class to recover, which prevents rapid down/up transitions on marginal links.
For links that are already close to threshold, raise the packet-loss threshold by 1 to 2 percent to avoid unnecessary path switching.
Keep the probe interval at 1000 ms for voice or other latency-sensitive classes unless a site-specific design requires a slower cadence.
commands: app-route sla-class voice loss-threshold 5 latency-threshold 80 probe-interval 1000 hold-down 5000

sections.heading: Certificate chain maintenance and edge re-registration
key_facts: Reimport the full certificate chain, including the active intermediate CA, on the orchestrator before renewing any edge certificate.
Stage the new chain at least 24 hours before the old intermediate expires so renewal and re-registration do not fail during the cutover window.
If edge re-registration fails after renewal, verify that the orchestrator trust bundle contains the current intermediate and root chain in the same import set.

sections.heading: Policy push limits, CRL freshness, and route-map sizing
key_facts: Keep each route-map at 256 entries or fewer; split larger maps into separate policy objects before the push.
If a tenant already has a larger route-map, remove 10 to 20 entries, commit the change, and re-add the remainder in a second commit to unblock policy push.
Refresh the CRL before it is older than 24 hours, or align CA publication to a 12 to 18 hour interval so the push window does not hit the hard-expiry check.
Confirm the updated CRL timestamp before retrying a failed policy push.

sections.heading: LTE tunnel MTU and handoff tuning
key_facts: After any 3.1 upgrade, reapply the LTE tunnel MTU on each dual-SIM edge because the upgrade may rewrite it to 1500.
For most carrier LTE links, use a tunnel MTU between 1400 and 1420 bytes; validate the path with 1472-byte pings before returning the site to service.
On 3.2 systems with custom APN profiles, recheck every LTE interface after migration because the per-interface tunnel MTU can be dropped.
For 3.3 edges with both modems enabled, set the LTE handoff debounce to 5000 ms to reduce CPU spikes during transient signal loss.

sections.heading: Overlay tunnel queueing and routing-cache hygiene
key_facts: Place SLA probes into a high-priority queue on busy links so burst traffic does not delay probe packets and flap the overlay tunnel.
If shaping is already enabled, reduce the bulk-traffic class to 60 to 70 percent so control traffic is not queued behind large data bursts.
After a planned underlay withdrawal, trigger a route-refresh or shorten the app-route cache age-time to 60 seconds during the maintenance window.
Confirm that withdrawn routes disappear from the cache before moving traffic to the backup link.

sections.heading: Reporting load control and operational verification
key_facts: Reduce flow-history retention to 5 days when reporting jobs are consuming excessive CPU on 3.3 systems.
If the environment requires longer retention, split reports into narrower 24-hour jobs and schedule them during a low-change maintenance window.
Use reporting window changes to avoid contention with policy updates on the same CPU cores.
Verify tunnel state and application-route status after report tuning so operational troubleshooting is not confused by delayed analytics processing.
